Definition: properly, deferred, i.e. the morrow; usually (adverbially) tomorrow; indefinitely, hereafter
BiblicalUsage: The word means tomorrow, the morrow, and it is the word of God's appointments. Pharaoh said tomorrow for the frogs to be removed, and Moses said tomorrow the LORD would bring the locusts, and the manna was kept until the morning. Saul was told that tomorrow about this time God would send the man to be captain over Israel, and Joshua told the people to sanctify themselves, for tomorrow the LORD would do wonders among them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe tomorrow is God's word, not ours, because every tomorrow in Scripture arrives on His appointment and not a moment sooner. I hold that the manna teaches us to wait for tomorrow's bread, and the wonders God promises for tomorrow are worth sanctifying ourselves for today.
